item.title: Gemini 4 Neon Undercuts Its Big Brother as AI Models Start Looping
item.description: Google's new mid-tier model nearly matches its flagship for half the price, and three labs bet on a stranger way to build AI.

item.title: Today on the Island: Storytime, Tai Chi and 21 Guns
item.description: Library storytime in the morning, two Tai Chi classes at the Recreation Center, and 21 Guns at Narragansett Café at 8:15 PM.

item.title: Tree Lighting and Concert Dec. 5 Caps the Holiday Stroll
item.description: The island lights its Christmas tree at East Ferry Wharf from 5:30 to 7 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 5, after a full day of the Holiday Stroll and Santa's arrival by boat.

item.title: Fusion Has Record Money. It Still Needs $80 Billion More.
item.description: A new global outlook counts more fusion machines and more private cash than ever, and a long, expensive road before any of it lights your kitchen.

item.title: Cliff Booth Is Back, and He Only Plays in IMAX for Two Weeks
item.description: David Fincher directs Brad Pitt in a Quentin Tarantino script that picks up eight years after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, opening in IMAX Wednesday.

item.title: Waymo Takes the Exit: Robotaxis Pulled Off Highways in Five Metros
item.description: After California called its driverless highway runs a public safety hazard, Waymo stopped highway rides everywhere it offered them, with no restart date.

item.title: Xpeng Puts Its Iron Humanoid on Stage Wednesday. The Clock Is Ticking
item.description: The Chinese EV maker's AI Day on Nov. 25 is its last big show before its own deadline to mass-produce a walking robot.

item.title: The Fockers Crash Thanksgiving, Up Against Disney and Haymitch
item.description: Focker-In-Law opens Wednesday against Disney's Hexed and a second weekend of the new Hunger Games.

item.title: Haymitch Gets His Origin Story as Hunger Games Returns to Theaters
item.description: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters, with trackers betting it opens bigger than any Hunger Games film in a decade.

item.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Aim at Office Work, for Less
item.description: OpenAI's two new models promise better documents, code and design work at lower prices, as the race with Anthropic and Google tightens.

item.title: Voyager 1 Is Now One Light-Day From Earth
item.description: After more than 49 years in flight, NASA's farthest spacecraft has crossed a distance light needs a full day to travel.

item.title: Mrs. Claus and Dickens Carolers Sail From East Ferry
item.description: Coastal Queen Cruises runs a Candy Cane Express with Mrs. Claus on Sunday, Nov. 29, and a carolers cruise on Saturday, Dec. 5, both from 1 East Ferry Wharf.

item.title: Library Book Sale and Yarn Swap on Holiday Stroll Day
item.description: The Friends of the Jamestown Philomenian Library hold their Winter Book Sale at the library during the Holiday Stroll on Saturday, Dec. 5.

item.title: Rock and Blues All Thanksgiving Week at the Ganny
item.description: The Narragansett Cafe, 25 Narragansett Ave., has live bands from Saturday, Nov. 21, through Sunday, Nov. 29, including the night before Thanksgiving.

item.title: An Evening of Kirtan at Island Heron Yoga on Dec. 5
item.description: Lisa Rubchinsky and Sarah Loomis lead call-and-response chanting Saturday, Dec. 5, 6 to 7:30 p.m., at 34 Narragansett Avenue.

item.title: Baby Jam at the Library: Lap Songs for Babies Up to 24 Months
item.description: The Jamestown Philomenian Library's Tuesday lap-sit session brings stories, finger rhymes and small-instrument songs to the youngest island families.

item.title: Electric Bills Could Drop Up to 75% Under New Rhode Island Energy Discount
item.description: Five income-based discount levels from 10% to 75% replace the current 25% and 30% discounts, starting in early 2027.

item.title: After-School Wheel Throwing for Grades 3 to 6
item.description: A Nov. 16–25 Arts After School session teaches the basics of wheel throwing, and a mixed-media series follows.

item.title: Out of the Box's Artists-in-Residence Show Runs to Dec. 31
item.description: More than 30 artists in residence share one collaborative show at the studio and gallery on Clinton Avenue, open from Aug. 8 through Dec. 31.

item.title: Get the Jamestown Island News App
item.description: Put Jamestown Island News on your phone's home screen or your computer's desktop and open it with one tap, like any other app.

item.title: Santa and Mrs. Claus to Arrive by Sea for Jamestown's Village Holiday Stroll
item.description: The Coastal Queen docks at East Ferry Wharf at 1 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 5. A fire truck carries Santa and Mrs. Claus up to the Conanicut Gift Shop for photos from 1 to 2 p.m.

item.title: November at the Narragansett Cafe: A Band Almost Every Night
item.description: The Senders, 3 Wheelin, Deep End, the Strumdawgs, Jury Band and Don't Think Twice lead a packed month at 25 Narragansett Ave.

item.title: Jamestown Community Chorus Sings 'A Contemporary Christmas'
item.description: Two December concerts at the Recreation Center, Dec. 12 at 4 p.m. and Dec. 13 at 3 p.m., with mostly 21st-century music.

item.title: The Everybody Chorus Is Rockin' the '70s. Anyone Can Join
item.description: No auditions, all ages, Saturday mornings at the Recreation Center, and the money for music books goes to charity.

item.title: Holiday Cruises from Jamestown: Mrs. Claus, Carolers and the Bay at Christmas
item.description: The Coastal Queen runs a Candy Cane Express with Mrs. Claus on Nov. 29 and a caroling cruise from East Ferry right after Santa docks on Dec. 5.

item.title: Off-Season on the Island: Ferry's Done, Here's What's Open

item.title: Thanksgiving on the Island: How to Help Jamestown's Food Pantries
item.description: The Community Food Pantry and St. Mark's pantry are open through the holidays. Here's what they need and when to drop it off.

item.title: Last Call for Golf on Conanicus Avenue: Season Runs Through November
item.description: The Jamestown Golf Course's season runs April through the end of November, so there are still a few weeks to play the nine holes by the bay.

item.title: End of an Era: Island Rubbish Proposed Sale

item.title: Senior Center Heads Home to West Street
item.description: Senior services move back into the renovated building in early November, and a Nov. 2 hearing could open the door to a north-end fire station.
